predecessors.note: 'In 1381, he took over Eretnid lands and claimed the title of sultan for himself' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page); the regent 'proclaimed himself as the ruler by January 1381' (Eretnids page).

successors.note: 'Burhan al-Din's son sought help from Bayezid I ... Consequently, the territories of the Burhan al-Din state came under Bayezid's control' (Kadi Burhan al-Din page).

capitals.name: Sivas
capitals.note: 'declared his sovereignty in Sivas' (1381); 'Burhan al-Din was interred ... in Sivas'. The infobox places his death at Erzincan and the page says the Eretnid capital was 'initially Erzincan, later moving to Kayseri'.

rulers.name: Kadi Burhan al-Din
rulers.title: sultan
rulers.note: Infobox reign 1381-1398; born 8 January 1345 at Kayseri; 'In 1398, Burhan al-Din was killed in the Karabel region during a battle with Qara Yuluk Osman'.

rulers.name: Zayn al-Abidin
rulers.note: The page says he 'ruled the principality between 1398 and 1399' and elsewhere 'reigned for a few weeks after his father's demise'; the Ottomans 'soon captured Sivas'.

correction.text: the Eretnid lands left in 1380-1381 with Amasya

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state). 1381: 'he took over Eretnid lands'; 'Later that year, Burhan al-Din defeated his main rival, Haji Shadgeldi of Amasya, and declared his sovereignty in Sivas.' The page says he 'successfully restored the former borders of his beylik' and names Kayseri (reclaimed 1378), Kırşehir, Malatya and a push 'as far as Ankara and Sivrihisar', all undated, so only the 1380-1381 Eretnid core (the Eretnids dossier's 1378 lands) with Amasya is drawn.

region.text: the Eretnid lands left in 1380-1381 (the 1378 realm without Amasya, Niğde, Aksaray, Ankara and the east)

ledger.note: 1381: 'In 1381, he took over Eretnid lands and claimed the title of sultan for himself.' The Eretnids page: Ala al-Din Ali died in August 1380 and the regent Kadi Burhan al-Din 'proclaimed himself as the ruler by January 1381'. He had been made vizier by the Eretnid emirs and had reclaimed Kayseri in 1378.
1381: 'Later that year, Burhan al-Din defeated his main rival, Haji Shadgeldi of Amasya, and declared his sovereignty in Sivas.' The page does not say in so many words that Amasya was taken.

region.text: the Eretnid lands left in 1380-1381 with Amasya

ledger.note: 1398: Burhan al-Din is killed in July-August 1398 fighting Qara Yuluk Osman; his son 'sought help from Bayezid I, who dispatched his eldest son with an army of 40,000 troops. Consequently, the territories of the Burhan al-Din state came under Bayezid's control.' The page also says Zeynal ruled 1398-1399 and that 'the Ottomans soon captured Sivas'.

region.text: the Eretnid lands left in 1380-1381 with Amasya

ledger.note: 1398: the state ends with Burhan al-Din's death (infobox reign 1381-1398); Zeynal's weeks of rule run into 1399 on one sentence.

wars.name: Mamluk campaigns against Burhan al-Din
wars.outcome: 'Burhan al-Dīn was defeated by the Mamluks in 1387 but soon allied with them'; 'the Mamluk army laid siege to Sivas for several months in 1388 but failed to defeat Burhan al-Din'. The page ties the quarrel to his capture of Malatya.

wars.name: Ottoman campaigns against Burhan al-Din
wars.outcome: 'That same year [1390], Bayezid launched several campaigns against him, capturing some fortresses and cities'; none is named.

wars.name: Battle with Qara Yuluk Osman
wars.outcome: Burhan al-Din 'was killed in the Karabel region during a battle with Qara Yuluk Osman' (July-August 1398; the Ottoman historian Saadeddin places it 'in the Harput Mountains'). The Ottomans then took his lands.

certainty.note: Only the Eretnid core is drawn. Kırşehir, Malatya and the advance to Ankara and Sivrihisar are on the page without dates; the Ottomans' fortresses of 1390 are unnamed. Provincial outlines stand in for towns.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened (Kadi Burhan al-Din, Eretnids), the latter shared with the eretnids dossier. The article is the biography of the ruler; 'Burhan al-Din state' is the page's own phrase for the territory. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Territory: the page lists a restored 'former borders', Kırşehir and Malatya (captured, undated) and an advance 'as far as Ankara and Sivrihisar'; none is dated, so the dossier draws the Eretnid core of 1380-1381 plus Amasya and says so under certainty. Rulers: Burhan al-Din 1381-1398; his son Zayn al-Abidin 'ruled the principality between 1398 and 1399' on one sentence and 'a few weeks' on another.
Status: 'in 1397, he sought assistance from his former adversary, the Mamluk Sultan ... offering to become a Mamluk vassal in return'; the 1387 defeat was followed by an alliance, not a dated vassalage (the flag 'Mamluk vassal 1387' in another report is not on the page). Vassal events would belong to mamluk-sultanate and are not recorded.
Mirrors: the ottoman-empire dossier gains the Sivas region in 1395 from 'Anatolian beyliks of the Sivas region' at confidence 1 and carries no 1398 gain from this state; Timur's entry to Anatolia in early 1394 'reaching Erzurum' is on the page without a result for Sivas. The aq-qoyunlu dossier has no 1398 war with Burhan al-Din. The infobox puts his death at Erzincan while the lead says Sivas.
Gazetteer names used that it may lack: Şebinkarahisar (place).
